move: lines slam in stepped, clip-path slices tear lime and pink, stepped exit
how: A square dark frame with a tilted lime stripe drifting xPercent -8 to 8 linearly across the 2s, a small top caption, three stacked uppercase lines in white and a lime meta row. Each line carries two absolutely-positioned coloured copies (lime and pink, screen-blended). Lines slam in alternately from xPercent -60 / 60 with steps(5) over 0.3s starting at 4% and every 0.16s; for six 0.055s ticks after each landing the copies are set to random horizontal clip-path inset bands shifted up to 45px either way, then hidden, so slices of colour tear off and snap back. At 57% a single twitch repeats one slice on every line with an 8px jolt. From 83% the lines exit the opposite way with steps(4) and the meta and caption cut out in steps(2), ending on the drifting stripe.
adapt: Change the three line strings (each needs its two .s copies), the caption and meta words, and the lime/pink pair; the stripe colour and angle. Keep the steps() eases and the 0.055s slice cadence; regenerate slice bands from a seeded rng so the render is deterministic.
port: mount(el, shot) builds stripe, top, the .line stack with .s.a/.s.b copies from shot.lines and the .meta row; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with each line at (0.08+i*0.16)/2*D, its six set() ticks, the twitch at 0.575D and the exit at 0.83D, using fx-style seeded rng for the clip bands. Scope gsap.utils.toArray('.line') to el.
caveats: uses many timeline set() calls; fine, but they must be placed at absolute times not chained
